key_insight: Finite-time Lagrangian transport structures in the mid-plane of a reacting supersonic shear layer strongly organize scalar gradients and align with regions of intense stretching.
engineering_relevance: The results help identify where mixing and reaction are concentrated in compressible turbulent flows, supporting better diagnostics and model development for reacting shear layers.
method: Compute forward/backward FTLE fields from time-resolved mid-plane DNS data.
Extract ridge skeletons and compare them with hyperbolic geodesic LCS from planar Cauchy-Green tensors.
Quantify ridge overlap, persistence, scalar conditioning, and lag relative to transport and decorrelation scales.
evidence_signal: The study uses time-resolved mid-plane data from a 3D DNS of a supersonic hydrogen-air temporal mixing layer and evaluates transport using FTLE ridges, Cauchy-Green measures, geodesic LCS, and scalar-conditioned statistics.
watch_item: Because the analysis is based on a constrained 2D slice and finite-time integration, the inferred transport skeleton may not fully capture three-dimensional or longer-time dynamics.
paper_title: Planar Lagrangian transport and scalar-gradient organization in a turbulent reacting shear layer
